facts: An implementation of data-driven selection of emphatic facial displays for an embodied conversational agent in a dialogue system is described.
A corpus of sentences in the domain of the target dialogue system was recorded.
The facial displays used by the speaker were annotated.
The data from those recordings was used in a range of models for generating facial displays.
Each model made use of a different amount of context or chose displays differently within a context.
The models were evaluated in two ways.
The models were evaluated by cross-validation against the corpus.
The models were evaluated by asking users to rate the output.
The predictions of the cross-validation study differed from the actual user ratings.
The cross-validation gave the highest scores to models making a majority choice within a context.
The user study showed a significant preference for models that produced more variation.
The preference for models that produced more variation was especially strong among the female subjects.
